question: A researcher has fifteen sets of interview notes and must produce a findings section for a report. Which sequence of stages should she follow?
options: A) Check each theme against the notes; pull the relevant extracts from each set of notes; write the findings section; group the extracts into themes.
B) Group the extracts into themes; check each theme against the notes; write the findings section; pull the relevant extracts from each set of notes.
C) Pull the relevant extracts from each set of notes; group the extracts into themes; check each theme against the notes; write the findings section.
D) Write the findings section; group the extracts into themes; pull the relevant extracts from each set of notes; check each theme against the notes.
correct_answers: C) Pull the relevant extracts from each set of notes; group the extracts into themes; check each theme against the notes; write the findings section.
explanations: Checking themes that have not yet been formed is not possible, and grouping after the section is written leaves the writing unsupported.
Themes cannot be grouped before the extracts have been pulled, so this ordering starts from material that has not been gathered.

Correct. Extracts come out of the notes first, grouping turns them into themes, the check confirms each theme is genuinely supported before it becomes a claim, and the section is written last from verified material.
Findings written before the extracts exist are assertions in search of evidence, and the checking stage arrives after the section is already written.
